name: personal code
issuer: the Lithuanian population register (the sheet names no office)
note: Lithuania's sheet (its government's own sheet on the OECD's automatic-exchange portal ('Information on Tax Identification Numbers'; the OECD's index page sits behind a bot check and wasn't opened, the sheet itself came straight back)), read 2026-10-30: the TIN of a natural person equals the Lithuanian personal code, immutable for life: 11 digits, the first (1 to 6) giving sex and century, then the birth date, and an eleventh check digit by weights the sheet spells out (the game doesn't compute it yet, `check` left out). Individuals get it automatically. The sheet doesn't name the office that gives it. Read as given at birth, to residents. No fee or time is stated.

sources.title: OECD AEOI portal, Lithuania: Information on Tax Identification Numbers (the jurisdiction's own sheet)
sources.said: Natural persons: In Lithuania the TIN equals the Lithuanian personal code. This code is immutable throughout the life of the natural person. ... C1 Can only take the value 1 to 6. C2, C3 Two last digits of a year. ... Individuals [Yes] Entities [Yes]
